Title: Arid Logics studio receives a Tulane Prize Honorable Achievement
Teaser: Kathy Velikov's thesis seminar and studio on the Las Vegas Valley is recognized for climate change curriculum.
BodyHTML:
Arid Logics: Climate Coexistence in Desert America, the thesis seminar and studio taught by Kathy Velikov at Taubman College, received an Honorable Achievement in the Innovative Studio Pedagogy category of the 2026 Tulane Prize for Climate Change Curriculum in the Built Environment.

The prize is given by the Tulane Center on Climate Change and Urbanism. The studio worked on the Las Vegas Valley.

Title: Responsive Envelopes | Regional Transitions: lecture at the University of Innsbruck
Teaser: Kathy Velikov and Geoffrey Thün present RVTR's work in the Structure and Digital Design Lecture Series 2026.
BodyHTML:
Kathy Velikov and Geoffrey Thün gave the guest lecture "Responsive Envelopes | Regional Transitions" at the University of Innsbruck, as part of the Structure and Digital Design Lecture Series 2026.

The lecture page describes RVTR as a platform to advance environmentally adaptive, technologically enabled and climate-positive built environments, supported by federal agencies, philanthropies and industry partners. The title names two lines of the lab's research: responsive envelopes and regional transitions.

Title: When It Rains, It Floods: Portico on the Southeast Michigan stormwater project
Teaser: Taubman College's Portico covers the nature-based stormwater strategy for Southeast Michigan.
BodyHTML:
Portico, published by Taubman College, ran "When It Rains, It Floods", a feature on the regional stormwater project funded by the National Fish and Wildlife Foundation. Kathy Velikov is co-principal investigator of the Taubman College component, and Geoffrey Thün is a collaborator.

The project's advisory workshops involved 36 organizations. "Urban flooding is a complex problem," Velikov says in the article, and the work requires "transdisciplinary collaborations." Thün describes a pan-sector model that can "create strong connections" between research and community impact.

Title: Institute for Advanced Construction Futures funded, directed by Kathy Velikov
Teaser: One of the first ten University of Michigan Impact Institutes, with Velikov as director.
BodyHTML:
The Institute for Advanced Construction Futures (IACF), directed by Kathy Velikov, is one of the first ten University of Michigan Impact Institutes. Geoffrey Thün is among its co-investigators.

The institute received $200,000 over two years from the university's Strategic Initiative Fund to advance low-carbon "Construction 4.0".

Title: "Stretch Codes and the Building Envelope" published in TAD 9:1
Teaser: A review of U.S. and Canadian energy stretch codes and what they mean for building envelopes and embodied carbon.
BodyHTML:
"Stretch Codes and the Building Envelope", by Kathy Velikov, Hasan, Lewis, Menassa, Kamat and Geoffrey Thün, appears in TAD 9:1, pages 156–171.

The article reviews energy stretch codes in the United States and Canada and their implications for building envelopes and embodied carbon.

Title: Kathy Velikov elevated to the AIA College of Fellows
Teaser: The American Institute of Architects elevates Kathy Velikov to its College of Fellows.
BodyHTML:
Kathy Velikov, Professor of Architecture and Associate Dean for Research and Creative Practice at Taubman College and a director of RVTR, has been elevated to the American Institute of Architects College of Fellows. According to the college's announcement, fewer than 3 percent of architects hold the fellowship.

The fellowship recognizes her for "furthering the science and art of planning and building by advancing the standards of architectural education and training." Her work spans practice-based design research toward environmentally responsive, technologically enabled and climate-positive built environments, from responsive material assemblies to territorial practices for decarbonization.

"I am truly honored to be recognized for my work by the AIA and the distinguished jury of peers," Velikov said. The new fellows were honored at AIA25 in Boston, June 4–6, 2025.

Title: NFWF grant for a nature-based stormwater strategy in Southeast Michigan
Teaser: A National Coastal Resilience Fund grant supports a regional plan combining nature-based and grey infrastructure.
BodyHTML:
Taubman College faculty, including Kathy Velikov as co-principal investigator and Geoffrey Thün, are part of a multi-institution team developing a regional stormwater plan for Southeast Michigan. The plan combines nature-based solutions with grey infrastructure to reduce flooding and enhance biodiversity.

The work is funded by a National Fish and Wildlife Foundation National Coastal Resilience Fund grant of $499,300, with $500,000 in cost share, and runs from 2024 to 2026. Partners include Wayne State University, Michigan State University and LimnoTech.

"Stormwater flooding is a major threat to communities of Southeast Michigan," Velikov said.

Title: Becoming Biomass in Regional Globalism in the Tennessee Valley
Teaser: RVTR and POST's speculative project on the Tennessee Valley opens at the Ewing Gallery, University of Tennessee, Knoxville.
BodyHTML:
Becoming Biomass, by RVTR (Geoffrey Thün and Kathy Velikov) and POST (Ersela Kripa and Stephen Mueller), was an invited project in the exhibition Regional Globalism in the Tennessee Valley at the Ewing Gallery, University of Tennessee, Knoxville, from November 4 to December 4, 2024.

The project envisions a cooperative-managed agroforestry and biomanufacturing transformation of the Tennessee Valley as part of a near-future U.S. decarbonization. Mappings, drawings, models and two silent films depict the actors in this transformation, from lignin and lands to infrastructures and a biorefinery.

Title: Geoffrey Thün gives keynote at the Facade Tectonics 2024 World Congress
Teaser: "Responsive Envelopes: Paradigms and Potentials", a keynote on RVTR's envelope research.
BodyHTML:
Geoffrey Thün delivered the keynote "Responsive Envelopes: Paradigms and Potentials" at the Facade Tectonics 2024 World Congress.

Responsive envelopes have been a line of RVTR's research since North House, through full-scale prototypes including The Stratus Project, Resonant Chamber, Pneusystems and Infundibuliforms.

Title: NextHouse receives an NSF Engines Development Award
Teaser: A $1 million National Science Foundation award for next-generation factory-built housing, with the University of Michigan as a partner.
BodyHTML:
NextHouse, an initiative on next-generation factory-built housing, received a $1 million NSF Engines Development Award from the National Science Foundation. The program is run by Purdue University, with the University of Michigan as a partner.

According to Geoffrey Thün's CV, the University of Michigan component is $115,000, with Thün as co-principal investigator. In 2023 the NextHouse proposal was named one of 34 semifinalists in the NSF Regional Innovation Engines program.

Title: Kathy Velikov receives the ACADIA Society Award for Leadership
Teaser: ACADIA's board recognizes Velikov's leadership of the organization, including her term as President.
BodyHTML:
The Association for Computer Aided Design in Architecture (ACADIA) gave Kathy Velikov its 2023 Society Award for Leadership, for "extraordinary contributions and service to the ACADIA community". The jury citation states: "This award recognizes the significant role that Kathy Velikov has played in ACADIA's leadership."

Velikov was President of ACADIA from 2018 to 2020 and Vice President from 2021 to 2022. As President she created the ACADIA Diversity Committee and updated its publication ethics. She was Technical Co-Chair of ACADIA 2016, Posthuman Frontiers, at the University of Michigan.

She gave the award talk, "Cultivating a Community of Practice", on October 26, 2023.

Title: From Matter to Territory: lecture at Syracuse University
Teaser: Kathy Velikov and Geoffrey Thün lecture at the Syracuse University School of Architecture.
BodyHTML:
Kathy Velikov and Geoffrey Thün gave the lecture "From Matter to Territory" at the Syracuse University School of Architecture.

Velikov has given lectures under the same title at CU Denver (February 2021, with Thün) and as a keynote at Georgia Tech's Divergence in Architectural Research (March 2020).
Source: https://soa.syr.edu/live/profiles/1154-kathy-velikov; date from Kathy Velikov's FAIA submission (lecture list)

Title: Ambiguous Territory: Architecture, Landscape, and the Postnatural published by Actar
Teaser: The book of the exhibition and symposium co-curated by Kathy Velikov, co-edited with Cathryn Dwyre, Chris Perry and David Salomon.
BodyHTML:
Ambiguous Territory: Architecture, Landscape, and the Postnatural, edited by Cathryn Dwyre, Chris Perry, David Salomon and Kathy Velikov, is published by Actar (256 pages). It has a foreword by Catherine Ingraham and an afterword by Peder Anker.

The book follows the exhibition and symposium of the same name, which assembled more than forty projects by architects, landscape architects and artists whose work challenges the division between the built and the natural environment. The exhibition was shown at Taubman College (2017), the University of Virginia (2018), Pratt Manhattan Gallery (2018–2019) and Ithaca College (2019), each with a public symposium.

The book was launched at Rizzoli Bookstore in New York in January 2023. Its print run of 1,500 copies sold out.
Source: https://actar.com/product/ambiguous-territory/; exhibition venues and print run from Kathy Velikov's FAIA submission

Title: Kathy Velikov named Associate Dean for Research and Creative Practice
Teaser: Velikov succeeds Geoffrey Thün as Taubman College's Associate Dean for Research and Creative Practice.
BodyHTML:
Taubman College named Kathy Velikov Associate Dean for Research and Creative Practice, succeeding Geoffrey Thün. Earlier in 2021 she was promoted to Professor of Architecture.

"I look forward to helping elevate and advance the multiple facets of research and creative practice at Taubman College," Velikov said.

Title: Geoffrey Thün appointed Associate Vice President for Research
Teaser: Thün joins the University of Michigan's research leadership for the social sciences, humanities and the arts.
BodyHTML:
The University of Michigan Regents approved the appointment of Geoffrey Thün as Associate Vice President for Research: Social Sciences, Humanities, and the Arts, in the Office of the Vice President for Research.

"It is an honor to join the OVPR team and serve the U-M research community," Thün said, adding that "a transdisciplinary approach is anticipated to be at the core of advancing research impacts."

Title: EXTRACTION opens in the Canadian Pavilion at the 2016 Venice Architecture Biennale
Teaser: RVTR is part of the team representing Canada at the 15th Venice Architecture Biennale.
BodyHTML:
EXTRACTION, curated by Pierre Bélanger (OPSYS), opened in the Canadian Pavilion at the 15th Venice Architecture Biennale, running from May 27 to November 27, 2016. The commissioner was the Art Gallery of Alberta (Catherine Crowston). RVTR's team was Geoffrey Thün, Kathy Velikov and Colin Ripley, with research assistants Jen Ng, Andrew Wald, Dan Tish and Ya Suo.

The project, an installation, film and book, examines Canada's resource extraction. It was selected through a national competition by a Canada Council for the Arts peer committee, announced in December 2015.

EXTRACTION later received the 2017 AZ Award for Social Good and a 2017 CSLA National Award of Excellence.
